It is known issue that Linux doesn't play well with some of the newer Acer BIOS. If you trying to get a new Linux install working you might need to downgrade.

So you go over to Acer official site on your poopy Windows 10 pc and download the BIOS you need.I have an Acer Aspire E5. You extract it and run the .exe but alas, failure!? Where is this winslplash I'm suppose to have access to? Insyde...kay? Cue some bullshit about already having the newest version. Fuck that.

  • After you get the failure message, minimize the window ( don't close program). Make sure you deactivate hidden files. Go to:

C:\Users\<profile name>\AppData\Local\Temp

  • Look for a folder with random jumble letter and numbers that ends in .tmp.

  • Open that bitch up to make sure it's what you want. Should contain some files like H2OFFT-W.exe and zrt.rd.

  • Copy pasta that shit to desktop.

  • Now, close BIOS installation thingy-ma-duder.

  • Go into the folder you copypastad and look for platform.ini.

  • Open platform.ini in a text editor.

  • Look for something like this:

[BIOSVersionFormat]
;[nbh-version] +
BIOSVFEnable=1
VersionFormat=XN.NN

  • Change XN.NN to XN.DD and save.

  • Run H2OFFT-W. exe. Enjoy BIOS downgrade.

Disclaimer: I take no credit for this solution. I am a simple noob and discovered this in a random forum and wanted to share this with other struggling noobs.
